existing_tips: Accusative: 'ein' becomes 'einen' for masculine nouns – 'einen Wintermantel'.
'Die Blume' – feminine. '-e' ending often signals feminine gender.
'Lust haben' means 'to feel like' – 'Hast du Lust?' is a casual invitation.
'fünf gerade sein lassen' = to turn a blind eye / be lenient.
'seit' (since/for) always governs the dative case – no exceptions.
Yes/no question – verb takes V1 position. German doesn't need a 'do' auxiliary.
'Ob' (whether/if) introduces an indirect yes/no question – verb goes to the clause end.
Chant it: mit, aus, bei, nach, von, zu, seit, gegenüber. After any of these the article goes to dem
'Die Lehrerin' – feminine. '-in' suffix makes professions feminine.
